📋 Executive summary complete Recruitment is jointly caused by the cue and the response, shown at TWO fidelity levels. Phenomenological realization: the baseline recruits…

The reference vertical slice for the **Biological Claim Layer** — the proposal that a biological CLAIM (not an execution model) is the canonical source, with simulators as compile targets. Here a secreted chemotactic cue recruits responder cells, and recruitment requires BOTH the cue and a competent response. The claim, its mechanism, and its viva-cpm realization are authored as a backend-neutral bundle (investigations/chemotactic-recruitment/claim-bundle/). The claim is now carried by TWO realizations: the original PHENOMENOLOGICAL CPM realization (three studies, chemotaxis lambda a stand-in for the response) and a finer-grained RECEPTOR-LEVEL realization (two studies) in which the response is EMERGENT from a per-cell Hill receptor-occupancy model calibrated to a cited chemokine-receptor affinity. The semantic gap the first realization recorded is now closed by the second, not hidden. See the "Claim layer" figure and How-to-read below.

complete Current verdict. Recruitment is jointly caused by the cue and the response, shown at TWO fidelity levels. Phenomenological realization: the baseline recruits (recruitment index 0 -> 0.67, peak 0.83); blocking the response (lambda->0) or removing the cue (rate->0) each abolishes it (index stays at 0). Receptor-level realization: with the response made emergent from receptor occupancy (Kd 2.9 nM, CXCL8-CXCR1, Nasser 2009), the baseline still recruits (index 0.567, untuned) and blocking the response downstream of receptor binding abolishes it (0.067) -- grounding the response in a cited affinity and closing the recorded lambda-calibration gap.

Question. Does a secreted chemotactic cue drive directional migration and recruitment of responder cells into the source region, and does inhibiting the chemotactic response reduce that recruitment?

Hypothesis. In a Cellular Potts world where source cells secrete a diffusible field and responder cells chemotax up its gradient, responders will directionally migrate toward and accumulate near the source region. Removing either the cue or the response abolishes recruitment.

🧬 Biology — the mechanism this investigation models Many tissue behaviours reduce to a simple motif: one population emits a signal, another senses it and moves. Immune recruitment to a chemokine source, morphogen- guided…

Many tissue behaviours reduce to a simple motif: one population emits a signal, another senses it and moves. Immune recruitment to a chemokine source, morphogen- guided migration, and tumour-associated homing all share this secreted-cue -> directional-migration structure. Here we build the motif from first principles in a Cellular Potts model. Source cells continuously secrete a diffusible field that relaxes into a spatial gradient. Responder cells convert the local gradient into a bias on their membrane fluctuations (chemotaxis), so over many Monte-Carlo sweeps they drift up-gradient and accumulate at the source — they are recruited.

The investigation is designed as an argument, not a demo. The baseline establishes that the motif recruits. The intervention blocks the response while leaving the cue untouched, and recruitment vanishes — isolating the response as a necessary cause. The negative control removes the cue while leaving competent responders, and recruitment again vanishes — isolating the cue as the other necessary cause, and guarding against a metric that fires spuriously. The claim that survives all three is narrow and honest: within this domain, recruitment requires both a cue and a response, and the CPM chemotaxis term is a phenomenological stand-in for whatever receptor machinery a real system would use.

The receptor-level realization takes the next step: it replaces the "whatever receptor machinery" hand-wave with an actual, if minimal, one. Each responder now carries a per-cell receptor that reads its local cue concentration and computes fractional occupancy via a Hill relation whose half-maximum is a cited affinity (CXCL8 monomer-CXCR1, Kd = 2.9 nM, Nasser et al. 2009). A responder is naive and immotile until its occupancy crosses threshold; only then does it flip to an activated, chemotaxing type. The chemotactic response is therefore no longer a global knob set by hand -- it EMERGES cell-by-cell from receptor signaling. Making the response emergent surfaces two things the scalar lambda structurally cannot express. First, a CONCENTRATION THRESHOLD: recruitment is gated by whether the local cue clears the receptor's occupancy set-point, turning an arbitrary lambda into a falsifiable, dose-linked prediction anchored to a real Kd. Second, a SPATIAL ACTIVATION FRONT: responders nearer the source cross threshold first, so activation sweeps outward as a front rather than switching on uniformly -- a genuinely new readout (the activation-map figure) that a single lambda averages away. The receptor realization recruits at baseline (index 0.567, untuned) and, when the response is blocked downstream of receptor binding, recruitment collapses to 0.067 even though the receptors still bind the cue -- isolating the chemotactic RESPONSE, not mere receptor engagement, as the necessary cause, and reproducing the phenomenological realization's joint cue-and-response dependence at a higher fidelity. It remains a minimal model: two responder classes, a two-parameter occupancy relation, and a unit-mapping choice (conc_scale) that is recorded, not fit.

🔬 Scientific argument 5 for · 1 against A secreted chemotactic cue recruits responder cells to its source, and recruitment is jointly caused by the cue and a competent chemotactic response.…

Main claim. A secreted chemotactic cue recruits responder cells to its source, and recruitment is jointly caused by the cue and a competent chemotactic response. The claim holds at two fidelity levels: a phenomenological realization (the response is a chemotaxis-strength knob) and a receptor-level realization (the response is emergent from a cited chemokine-receptor occupancy).

Evidence for

  • Phenomenological baseline: recruitment index rises 0 -> 0.67 (peak 0.83), mean approach 0.61.
  • Phenomenological intervention (lambda=0): recruitment index stays at 0 with the cue present.
  • Negative control (rate=0): recruitment index stays at 0 with a competent response (shared by both realizations).
  • Receptor baseline: with the response emergent from receptor occupancy (Kd 2.9 nM, CXCL8-CXCR1, Nasser 2009), recruitment index reaches 0.567 (95% CI 0.345-0.788, 5 seeds), untuned.
  • Receptor intervention (response blocked downstream of receptor binding): recruitment index falls to 0.067 (95% CI 0.0-0.147), despite receptors still able to bind the cue.

Evidence against

  • None within the tested domain. Recruitment is response- and cue-dependent as predicted, in both realizations.

Caveats

  • In the PHENOMENOLOGICAL realization the CPM chemotaxis lambda is a response-strength stand-in (a bias on the copy-attempt energy), not a receptor-level model — a recorded semantic gap. The RECEPTOR realization closes it by making the response emergent from a per-cell Hill occupancy calibrated to a cited Kd; that Hill occupancy is still a minimal two-parameter model, not a full signaling cascade.
  • Receptor realization: the Kd (2.9 nM) is a cited real affinity, but conc_scale (CPM field-unit -> nM mapping), the Hill coefficient, and the activation-occupancy threshold remain recorded modeling choices (provenance: theory), not independently fit.
  • Field diffusion is capped (d<=0.25) for stability; the gradient is equilibrated before cell stepping, and responders are seeded within the gradient's reach.
  • Applicability: single secreted field, 2-D lattice, radius-based recruitment readout, a 6-cell slice. The phenomenological arm uses two cell types; the receptor arm adds a naive/activated responder sub-type. The response is now calibrated to a specific ligand/receptor system (CXCL8-CXCR1) only for the receptor realization.

🧬 recruitmentcue_rate=10 chemo_lambda=14

Biology

Cue + competent response recruits: across 5 independent seeds the final recruitment index is 0.767 +/- 0.170, versus 0.000 +/- 0.000 for both negative conditions (Cohen's d = 6.38). Recruitment is an emergent collective outcome of local chemotactic copy-attempt biases, not an engineered per-cell rule.

Overview

Simulate the CPM recruitment world (source slab + six responders in the gradient zone), equilibrate the secreted field, and measure the recruitment index — fraction of responders within 15 px of the source — over 500 MC sweeps. We recorded 1 finding confirm the expected biology. Gate decision: Passed. Gate cleared.

Model changes

Key assumptions

  • Same world geometry as recruitment-baseline (source slab + six responders, Moore-8 lattice, order 2).
  • Receptor occupancy is computed per responder each step from the local field via a Hill relation; activation is a one-way naive -> activated switch.
  • conc_scale maps the CPM field's raw amplitude into the Hill relation's nM-scale sensitive window; this mapping, not the Kd itself, is the simulation-unit calibration choice.
  • Recruitment radius = 15 px, identical to recruitment-baseline.

Conclusion synthesis

Read-only synthesis derived from the study's canonical fields (findings, limitations, follow-up proposals).

Claims
  • The receptor-level realization reproduces the baseline recruitment claim: across 5 seeds the final recruitment index is 0.5667 (95% CI 0.3451-0.7882), above the 0.5 pass threshold, with responder activation gated by a per-cell Hill-occupancy receptor model calibrated to a cited CXCL8-CXCR1 Kd rather than an arbitrary chemotaxis strength.
Evidence
  • recruitment index 0.5667 (95% CI 0.3451-0.7882) across 5 seeds, receptor-gated activation via a cited CXCR1 Kd (2.9 nM, Nasser 2009)
Next steps
  • Dose-response: recruitment vs receptor Kd and conc_scale

Biology

The intervention works in the receptor-level realization too: across 5 seeds the final recruitment index is 0.0667 (95% CI 0.0-0.1467) with the activated-type chemotaxis lambda forced to 0, versus 0.5667 for the receptor baseline -- recruitment remains response-dependent even when receptor binding itself is unaffected.

Overview

Repeat the receptor-recruitment world with blocked=True (the intervention) and measure the recruitment index over 500 MC sweeps across 5 seeds. We recorded 1 finding confirm the expected biology. Gate decision: Passed. Gate cleared.
